answer: Epoch nullifiers tie each seat to one scarce credential, such as an enclave key or a verified operator ID. Each epoch a seat posts a zero-knowledge proof plus a nullifier hashed from that credential and the epoch number, so two seats on one credential collide and are paid once. Credentials sit on a terrace of trust tiers, and each collision drops the credential one step. A saffron flag marks issuers whose credentials collide often; the canyon failure is an issuer selling keys in bulk, so a flagged issuer's whole tier is voided. Each fake needs its own live credential, re-proven every epoch.
